intended_object: Klein's modular invariant j, seen as a meromorphic function on the compactified level-one modular curve X(1) = PSL₂(ℤ)\ℍ ∪ {∞}, with a simple pole at the cusp. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: On the orbit quotient, the definition uses `jQuotient`, which is the descent of the library's `j z = E₄(z)^3 / Δ(z)` to the quotient by the image of PSL₂(ℤ). This is the standard normalized j-invariant. At the single cusp it gives the value 0. j has a pole there, so no complex value would be correct, and the 0 is a junk value. The docstring and the module documentation both say this openly. The library's notions of meromorphy and order only look at punctured neighbourhoods, so this value does not matter: the library goes on to prove that `jCompactified` is meromorphic everywhere and has order −1 at the cusp. The setting is the specific level-one curve X(1), and j is a specific object, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no j-invariant on ℍ and no j-invariant on a compactified modular curve.
